did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm’s heading indicates that it is intended for musical performance and attributes it to Asaph; it is described as both a “psalm” and a “song.”
Did you know? The psalm presents God’s name as renowned in Judah and Israel and emphasizes his greatness among his people.
Did you know? God’s dwelling place is described using two place names: “Salem” and “Zion.”
Did you know? This verse describes the breaking of various weapons of war: the arrows of the bow, the shield, the sword, and other weapons.
Did you know? God’s greatness is portrayed through light and majesty, and he is presented as more powerful than the “mountains of prey.”
Did you know? The enemy’s mighty warriors are described as having lost their strength and fallen asleep, so that the men of valor could not use their hands.
Did you know? The rebuke of the God of Jacob causes not only people but also chariot and horse to fall asleep—that is, the entire force of war.
Did you know? The psalm emphasizes that no one can stand before God when he reveals his anger; the description repeats the word “awesome.”
Did you know? God’s judgment is heard from heaven, and as a result the earth fears—and then becomes still.
Did you know? God’s rising to judge is presented as a means of saving “all the humble of the earth,” not merely as the defeat of his enemies.
